problem: Existing object navigation benchmarks place objects according to generic scene priors and ignore individual users' placement habits, so agents relying on commonsense fail when objects are placed idiosyncratically.
motivation: Home service robots must find objects placed by specific users, e.g. a book left on the sofa instead of in the study. Commonsense-driven LLM reasoning misguides exploration in such habit-shaped scenes, and long habit lists in prompts degrade small-LLM reasoning.
key_idea: Introduce UcON, a benchmark where objects are placed according to a large natural-language User Habit Knowledge Base, plus a RAG-style Habit Retrieval Module that selects target-relevant habits for the LLM prompt.
insight: Habits give explicit textual clues about non-obvious locations and improve LLM-based navigators, while the retrieval module beats the GT-habit setting in several rows (e.g. LGX LLaMA-3.1-8B GT detector 28.2 vs 20.4 SR, PixelNav LLaMA-3.1-8B 20.5 vs 17.2). The authors hypothesize this is because retrieved habits about other landmark objects (e.g. breakfast table) give useful context. Absolute SR stays low even with GT detection, which points to missing multi-step planning, exploration memory and belief updating. The encoder-only L3MVN cannot exploit habits.
method: UcON task: the agent is randomly placed in a habit-shaped OmniGibson scene (22 scenes), must find a target from 489 categories, and is given a habit KB of 300+ natural-language habits. Actions are MoveAhead 0.25 m, Rotate 90°, Look up/down 30°, Open, Done; 300-step limit; success = Done with target visible within 1 m.

Habit generation: a three-step GPT-4 pipeline generates habits and placements (nextto/onTop/inside/under), validates physical plausibility with the simulator API, then GPT-4 verifies semantic consistency between habit text and placement (~22,600 habits).
Habit-shaped scene: each episode samples 20 objects, adds all their habits to the KB, and places each object at one randomly chosen habit-specified position. Habits may conflict.
Habit Retrieval Module: BGE-M3 embeds the query 'Please retrieve the habit about {TargetObject}.' and all habits, and the top-p most similar habits are inserted into the LLM prompt.

Baselines adapted: PixelNav, LGX and L3MVN use GT object labels or YOLO-Worldv2-X and a GT path planner, with LLaMA-3.1-8B, LLaMA-3.2-11B-Vision or GPT-4 as the LLM. VTN and ZSON are end-to-end baselines.

Real-world validation: Unitree GO2 with an RGB-D camera, YOLO-Worldv2-X, a BFS planner and PixelNav, with the LLM run on an RTX 3090 workstation, in 3 environments (30 m² and 90 m²), evaluated as case studies.

setting.backbone: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct / LLaMA-3.2-11B-Vision / GPT-4 (frozen) with BGE-M3 retriever; L3MVN RoBERTa-Large; VTN and ZSON trained end-to-end
setting.training_data: none for the LLM-based methods (training-free); baselines VTN, ZSON and L3MVN are used as released or trained with unspecified details
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (simulated); GT object labels or YOLO-Worldv2-X detections
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MoveAhead 0.25 m, RotateLeft/Right 90°, LookUp/Down 30°, Open, Done (LLM-based methods pick directions or waypoints executed by a GT path planner)
setting.privileged: GT object labels for most rows and GT path planner; the GT-habit level uses habits directly related to the target

results: Habits consistently help LLM-based navigators: LGX with GPT-4 goes from 25.1 SR (no habits) to 30.6 with retrieval, and LGX with LLaMA-3.1-8B from 20.2 to 28.2. Retrieval usually beats Full habits and often beats GT habits. End-to-end VTN (2.1 SR) and ZSON (1.0 SR) fail, and L3MVN (10.6 SR) does not benefit from habits.
limitations: Habits are synthetic (GPT-4 generated) and may miss long-tail diversity and temporal drift; only plausibility is checked by a human study (98.5% habits, 96.7% placements judged plausible).

Focuses on habit utilization, not acquisition; the retrieval module is a simple proof-of-concept without context or uncertainty modelling; absolute SRs remain low; GT detectors and planners are used, and the real-world evaluation is only case studies against PixelNav.
